discussion_quotes.quote: The founder's framing: CDSFL striving to become a general-purpose STEM calculator, running on massively distributed compute and epistemic diversity, taking inspiration from Folding@home, Rosetta@home, SETI@home and Einstein@home without copying them.

Volunteer computing solves a specific problem: untrusted hosts. BOINC's design principle is that everything outside the project server is unreliable, possibly maliciously so. Its answer is replication ... The mechanism that matters here is homogeneous redundancy. ... It does this because floating-point differences between architectures produce disagreement that is noise -- an artefact of the substrate, not information about the answer.

CDSFL wants the opposite, and this is the entire distinction. Its coverage model (white paper Part XIII) states as Property 3 that when inter-architecture correlation rho = 1, coverage collapses: D(n) = D(1) for every n.

A distributed CDSFL that recruits fifty cognitive architectures to review one artefact is a distributed system doing the work of about four. That is the finding, and it is the opposite of the Folding@home shape.
No result is canonical by agreement. Where BOINC selects a canonical instance by quorum, a distributed CDSFL has no equivalent step.

Nothing described here has been built. The current system is five architectures reviewing one artefact at a time, with a load-balancing module that has never run outside its own tests and was shelved on 2026-08-22 for reporting an impossible allocation as a success.
FIGURE PROVENANCE, added 2026-09-10T20:55:12+01:00 under task 7.1. No artefact in bench/logs corresponds to this note, and no committed script reproduces its figures.

The current system is plumbing for structured adversarial code review. Good plumbing -- but not the original vision for Project Genesis: humans and machines cooperating and collaborating freely together, without borders and without restrictions.
The persistence layer becomes the live shared workspace -- not a post-hoc log. ... All participants read/write directly

(B) Distributed problem decomposition -- split a hard problem into many sub-problems, solve in parallel, recombine. This scales with compute; this is "1000 beats 5"; this is the "Global Mind." The paper does not model it and the system does not implement it. It is the dream behind the project, never designed.
THEN deliberately design architecture (B), the real Global Mind, on a tool-settled falsification core.

The production topology is currently a star: a central dispatcher co-ordinates a panel of heterogeneous models through a single connection gateway, so that each model interacts with the dispatcher rather than with every other model directly. Ring, mesh, hierarchical, hybrid, and configurable topologies remain open alternatives.

CDSFL trajectory is toward a distributed peer to peer architecture. ... The GlobalMind peer to peer compute sharing addresses this, but it is not built yet. ... Going from five models on one machine to a global peer to peer mesh is a very long road. Distributed systems are hard. Byzantine fault tolerance, incentive alignment, free rider problems, latency, trust.
We are facilitating adversarial review, where the natural unit of work is one model reads another's output and responds. That is inherently peer to peer.

Up to Experiment 32 the panel had been communicating through a central insect-brain relay -- models talking to models, each able to see the others' reasoning. Experiment 34 introduced the alternative: a structured blackboard ... Experiment 35 then made the choice a runtime switch. A single CLI flag, --topology relay|star, selects between the two.

It formalises the distributed compute hypothesis: that using multiple different AI architectures to review each other's work produces better defect detection than using copies of the same architecture.

modules_assuming_a_coordinator: bench/reference_runner_v3.py:2309 FindingRegistry - the obvious one, and worse than expected. Its docstring is 'Canonical finding registry - runner-owned, models read/propose only.' State is plain in-memory dicts (self.entries, self._alias_map) with NO durable or shared backing, and identity is a MONOTONIC COUNTER: line 2319 self._next_id = 1, line 2460 canonical_id = f'C{self._next_id:04d}'. A counter is a single-writer construct; two peers minting C0001 independently collide, and there is no merge rule. Lines 3500 and 3508 serialise next_id into and out of runner_state.json, so resume also assumes one authority holds the counter. A no-central-server mode needs content-addressed finding identity (sha256 of the canonical finding body, which bench/verification_chain.py already knows how to compute) in place of the counter.

bench/insect_brain.py:151 InsectBrain, with relay() at 223, relay_conversational() at 407, relay_directed() at 645 - the message bus. Imported unconditionally at bench/reference_runner_v3.py:247 and constructed per run (brain: InsectBrain threaded through at lines 10750, 10831, 15742). Every model-to-model message is a method call inside one process. There is no wire format, no addressing and no delivery semantics to replace it with gossip.

bench/dm/_manager.py plus bench/dm/_load_balancer.py and bench/dm/_role_assignment.py - the allocation layer assumes one allocator with global knowledge of every seat's token limit, cost, latency and current load. _load_balancer.py is shelved and unreachable (see built_artefacts), so there is not even a working single-coordinator allocator to distribute.

The convergence gate and gamma computation inside bench/reference_runner_v3.py - convergence is decided once, by the runner, from a registry it alone owns. A peer-to-peer mode has no agreed point at which the decision is taken, and the project's own rule forbids the obvious substitute: Scaling_Spec_GlobalMind_2026-08-26.md:105, 'Where BOINC selects a canonical instance by quorum, a distributed CDSFL has no equivalent step.'

The run directory itself - bench/logs/<run>/runner_state.json plus the per-seat JSON files are a local-filesystem shared-memory assumption. bench/star_topology_2026-10-06.py reads round_dir / 'BRIEF.md' and round_dir / f'{seat}.json' off local disk to decide whether a blind round LANDED; over a network that becomes a replication and conflict problem.

bench/seal_experiment_logs.py plus bench/verification_chain.py sealing - the epoch sealing step runs once, by one process, over a complete local log set. The VERIFY side is already decentralisable (content hashes, Ed25519, RFC 9162 inclusion proofs); the SEAL side is not.

The dispatch layer generally - zero networking exists. grep for socket, http.server, flask, fastapi, aiohttp, websocket, zmq, libp2p, kademlia across every .py in the tree returns matches in exactly 4 files, and all 4 use sockets to BLOCK network access in tests (bench/tests/conftest.py:84, bench/tests/netguard_plugin.py:52, bench/tests/test_suite_is_offline.py:68, bench/tests/test_free_window_cannot_spend_money_2026-08-30.py:25). The system is a single Python process on one Mac talking to vendor APIs.
helps_with_cold_start: "Yes, in 3 specific places, and I will mark the boundary where it stops helping. (1) IT REFRAMES THE 700-SEAT PREMISE WITH A NUMBER ALREADY IN THE RECORD. The founder's 2026-10-08 objection, quoted in bench/the_cold_start_cannot_use_a_tuple_at_scale_2026-10-08.py:6-9, is that the system must cope with '5, or 6, or 70, or 700 models'. Scaling_Spec_GlobalMind_2026-08-26.md:73 already answers what 700 seats on ONE artefact buys: 'A distributed CDSFL that recruits fifty cognitive architectures to review one artefact is a distributed system doing the work of about four', and its line 97 recommends 'Panel size fixed at 4-6, not scaled.' That arithmetic is the one part of the distributed work that is live and executing - bench/tests/test_scaling_spec_numbers_2026-08-26.py, 10 passed. So cold-start ranking over a 700-seat roster is an ALLOCATION-ACROSS-ARTEFACTS problem (the spec's Axis 2, line 79), not a fill-one-panel problem. That does not solve his ranking question, but it changes what a correct answer has to do. (2) THE VOLUNTEER-COMPUTING LITERATURE THE SPEC ALREADY IMPORTED HAS THE COLD-START REPUTATION ANSWER, AND THIS PROJECT HAS THE INSTRUMENT BUILT AND IDLE. Scaling_Spec_GlobalMind_2026-08-26.md:87: 'Spot-checking is what the planted-defect controls are. The technique sends workers occasional tasks whose correct answers are already known, and estimates each worker's credibility from what comes back.' Line 91: 'Adaptive replication has an analogue that is built and shelved. BOINC reduces replication for hosts with a track record of correct results. The survived-falsification ledger records that a claim was tested and stood, which is the raw material for exactly that. It was commissioned on 2026-08-25 and has never been used to vary anything.' A seeded-defect probe gives a capability estimate from WORK rather than from a name tuple, and it needs no history and no cross-seat overlap - which is exactly the property a cold start requires. The spec also states the one condition that would void it, line 103: 'Probes must be indistinguishable from work ... That requires the keys to live outside the artefact, outside the repository, and outside any inference from directory structure.' This project has already burned 5 experiments on that exact failure (line 87 names exp48, exp49, exp50, exp51, exp52 and the exp55 public-repository exposure). (3) THE ESTIMATOR IS ALREADY SPECIFIED IN THE RUNWAY AND IS WAITING ON A RECORDING CHANGE, NOT RESEARCH. experimental_notes/RUNWAY_to_BR2_2026-08-18.md:777 (item 0C.51): 'The scaling question is largely SOLVED prior art, and the blocker is a recording change ... Every estimator consumes exactly two numbers: findings seen by one reviewer (Q1) and by two (Q2). We record Q1 and have destroyed Q2 - OPEN - the fix is recording, not research.' Line 782 (item 0C.56) then answers the small-roster case directly: 'Change the sampling unit: the OCCASION, not the model, where occasion = (model, prompt-role, seed, round) ... Available at that tier: Good-Turing coverage over the sample axis, error seeding (no overlap required), and curve-fitting. The routing fix falls straight out: escalation at one model is RE-CONDITIONING - different role, seed, decomposition - not \"a stronger writer\".' And line 774 (item 0C.49) says why it was blocked: '2 of 2,050 real findings (0.10%) are recorded as raised by more than one model ... OPEN - HIGHEST, it gates the scaling work.' That block is PARTLY LIFTED since the runway was written: FindingRegistry.record_codiscovery now exists at bench/reference_runner_v3.py:2333, and on the founder's 2026-09-29 ruling its occasions record is read by _corroborated_novelty_series and feeds rho. WHERE IT STOPS HELPING, stated plainly. No peer-to-peer code was ever written, so there is nothing to reuse - the capability ranking cannot be lifted from a built distributed subsystem because none exists. The ledger has never varied anything, so 'the ledger can serve as the cold-start prior' is an UNTESTED claim, not a measured one. The spec's own figures carry a provenance warning (line 141) and may not be quoted as measurements - only the test's recomputed rho may. And the allocation module that would consume a capability ranking is shelved and reports impossible allocations as successes (bench/dm/_load_balancer.py:12-16), so a ranking delivered today has no live consumer."
verdict: "The discussion is real, it is substantial, and it survives in the record - but almost nothing was built, and what was built is a specification plus one passing test, not a system. 1. DOES THE DISCUSSION EXIST: yes, in 2 waves. The early wave is March and April 2026: docs/experimental_notes/CE_Distributed_Compute_Model_2026-03-19.md established that 'distributed compute' in this project means epistemic diversity, not network distribution; experimental_notes/Global_Mind_Architecture_2026-04-03.md set out a live shared workspace where 'All participants read/write directly' (line 39); the clearest peer-to-peer statement sits in an UNVERSIONED Desktop file, /Users/georgejackson/Desktop/CDSFL_tts/Perplexity_Revised_Assessment_2026-04-10.txt:48, 'The GlobalMind peer to peer compute sharing addresses this, but it is not built yet.' The late wave is 2026-08-26: experimental_notes/Scaling_Spec_GlobalMind_2026-08-26.md, 141 lines, is the most substantive artefact and it answers the founder's framing head on, naming Folding@home, Rosetta@home, SETI@home and Einstein@home at line 7 and BOINC's actual mechanism at lines 13-15. 2. WAS ANYTHING BUILT: not for peer-to-peer operation. Evidence I used to conclude it, not inference: the spec's own line 122, 'Nothing described here has been built'; zero hits across the whole tree for p2p, bittorrent, torrent, decentralis, serverless, gossip, dht, mesh-as-network, boinc-in-code or volunteer-in-code; and a networking census that found socket, http.server, flask, fastapi, aiohttp, websocket, zmq, libp2p and kademlia in exactly 4 files, all 4 of which use sockets to FORBID network access during tests. What WAS built: the spec, a 10-test guard that re-derives its numbers from the live archive and passes, the --topology star|relay switch (relay is a central relay, so still a coordinator), and bench/verification_chain.py. 3. ORPHAN OR LIVE: mixed, and the split matters. LIVE AND TESTED: the --topology flag (branched on at 5 sites in bench/reference_runner_v3.py), bench/verification_chain.py (imported by 9 modules, 2 dedicated test files), and the scaling test (10 passed in 1.71s, and it EXECUTES - it reads rho_history out of every run directory rather than asserting on prose). ORPHANED: bench/dm/_load_balancer.py, which says of itself 'It has never run outside its own tests' and whose own guard test asserts the quarantine. DOCUMENT-ONLY: the spec and bench/DISTRIBUTED_COMPUTE_PROTOCOL.md. AND A TRAP: bench/star_topology_2026-10-06.py is named for a topology but is confer-round discipline - do not cite it as network work. 4. ROADMAP: placed, and placed as deferred - the open-topology gap is runway item 36, 'My recommendation: Defer past BR2' (DECISIONS_AWAITING_YOU_2026-09-06.md:158-160), formally declared excluded from the executable task list at CDSFL_MASTER_TASK_LIST.md:537, and parked at CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md:1291. 5. WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE: the FindingRegistry is worse than 'the obvious one' - it is an in-memory dict with a monotonic C0001 counter at bench/reference_runner_v3.py:2460, which is a single-writer construct with no merge rule, and the fix is content-addressed finding identity, which verification_chain.py can already compute. Beyond it: the InsectBrain message bus is in-process method calls with no wire format; allocation assumes one allocator with global load knowledge and is shelved anyway; the convergence gate is decided once by the owner of the registry, and the project's own rule at spec line 105 forbids replacing that with a quorum; and the run directory is a local-filesystem shared memory. 6. ON THE IMMEDIATE PROBLEM: the archaeology helps indirectly but genuinely - see helps_with_cold_start. The single most useful thing I found is spec line 91, that the survived-falsification ledger is BOINC's adaptive-replication analogue, 'built and shelved ... commissioned on 2026-08-25 and has never been used to vary anything'. That is a capability prior derived from measured work rather than from model names, which is precisely what the founder objected to on 2026-10-08, and it is already in the tree. 7. ONE DOCUMENTARY DEFECT WORTH HIS ATTENTION: the only explicit peer-to-peer trajectory statement in the entire record exists in one unversioned file on one Desktop and was never mirrored into experimental_notes, whose 66-line repo counterpart contains none of it. By the project's own tts-output-protocol that mirror should exist."
